\newcommand{\HoldoutParagraph}{We ran the E9 holdout on four held-out concepts (water, green, thin, knitted; 50 trials at seed 1; linear and nonlinear plants) for the six candidates declared in the round-2 pre-registration plus $\ASS$ and $\ASF$, with the E9 pass rule (Table~\ref{tab:holdout}). Only M1 meets both $\tau$ thresholds. Under the registered flatness rule no candidate passes; that rule also fails for the oracle (above). Under the revised rule, M1 passes. Paired over trials (1000$\times$, seed 0), $\tau$(M1)$-\tau$($\ASF$) is 0.77 [0.71, 0.82] for the linear plant and 1.01 [0.96, 1.06] for the nonlinear plant, so M1 tracks the planted leakage better than $\ASF$ under both plants. M1 is given the concept score that defines the plant, while the AS-family scores are not, so this comparison favours M1 by construction. M1 was picked after the DEV results and the flatness rule was revised after the oracle test, so this holdout is post hoc. E9 stays a KILL as registered, and M1 is a candidate for a future pre-registered test, not a validated score.}
